brief: McElligott argues the S&P is simultaneously flat at the index level and in a rolling bear market underneath. The winning trade all year has been Long the AI Core Constraints (Semis plus Energy), up 65% YTD at a 3.2 Sharpe versus 8% for 60/40, because bonds have stopped working as either a long or a hedge. That narrowness drives record-low correlation and dispersion: ten stocks produced 70% of the rally, while most S&P sectors and 85% of names sit well off highs. Vol stays pinned because dealer gamma and structured-note vega supply keep selling it, so skew is extreme only on the upside: nobody hedges downside, everyone chases the right tail. The bull case needs AI capex trickle-down to lift the 'Other 493's' earnings. Two live tests followed: Trump pushed Iran strikes past the midterms (oil fell) though Iran reported new tanker mine strikes that evening, and the FT reported OpenAI's revenue is roughly $20bn below what it told investors, hitting the Nasdaq. McElligott still expects forced re-risking higher; the author thinks Goldman's correlation 'starburst' is more likely.
